title: Design CMS publishing with draft isolation and bounded freshness
businessContext: The CMS webhook invalidates every page and draft content sometimes appears in the public cache.
problemStatement: Design the system for 10,000 content routes; editors need immediate previews; public freshness under 60 seconds. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Bound invalidation fan-out and observe convergence.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 10,000 content routes; editors need immediate previews; public freshness under 60 seconds
functional: Bound invalidation fan-out and observe convergence.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Resolve CMS events through signature verification, durable event admission and a server-owned content/tag map.

Out-of-order publish/unpublish events can revive withdrawn content. Compare version/sequence semantics at the authoritative boundary and make unpublish/revocation propagation a distinct correctness requirement.
alternativeApproaches: In Next.js 16 updateTag is Server-Action-only. A Route Handler uses the documented revalidateTag profile; API context and chosen consistency semantics are both part of the design.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Replay, duplicate and reorder CMS events.
Warm public caches before opening an authenticated draft preview.
Unpublish content and measure removal from all supported regions and navigation paths.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
